q: 1. How much cement contained in one bag
explain: A standard bag of cement weighs 50 kg, which corresponds to a weight (force) of about 500 N (50 × 9.81 ≈ 490.5 N ≈ 500 N).

q: 2. The maximum quantity of ingredients present in cement production is
explain: Lime (CaO) forms the largest proportion (about 60-65%) of the chemical composition of cement, hence it is present in maximum quantity.

q: 3. The minimum percentage of chemical ingredient of cement is that of
explain: Magnesium oxide is a minor constituent and is present in the least percentage (about 1-3%) among all chemical ingredients of cement; its excess makes cement unsound.

q: 4. The characteristic, which makes the concrete a versatile and widely used material of modern construction, is the possibility of
options: controlling the properties of concrete by using appropriate ingredients
molding the concrete in any desired shape
complete mechanization of concrete preparation and its placing process
explain: Concrete's versatility comes from a combination of factors: controllable properties through mix design, moldability into any shape, and full mechanization of production and placement, all of which together make it widely used.

q: 5. In the manufacture of cement, the dry or wet mixture of calcareous and argillaceous materials is burnt at a temperature between
explain: In the kiln, the raw mixture of calcareous (limestone) and argillaceous (clay) materials is burnt at very high temperatures of about 1500°C to 1600°C to form clinker.

q: 6. Sieve analysis of portland cement is performed on IS sieve No.
explain: Fineness of Portland cement is tested by sieving on IS Sieve No. 9 (90 micron sieve) as per Indian Standard specifications.

q: 7. The percentage of gypsum added to the clinker during manufacturing process is
explain: Gypsum is typically added in the range of 0.35% to 5.0% by weight of clinker to regulate the setting time of cement.

q: 8. To perform the initial setting time test, the water is added to the cement at the rate of .... by weight of cement
explain: For the initial and final setting time tests, water is added at the rate of 0.85 times the water needed for standard consistency (P), i.e., 0.85P, as per IS code.

q: 9. An aggregate which passes through 25 m IS sieve and is retained on 20 mm sieve, is said to be flaky if its least dimension is less than
explain: For aggregate passing 25 mm and retained on 20 mm sieve (mean size 22.5 mm), it is classified as flaky if its least dimension (thickness) is less than 0.6 × mean size ≈ 13.5 mm; per the book's listed answer, however, the value taken corresponds to 22.5 mm as the flakiness gauge size reference.

q: 10. To perform the compressive strength test of cement, water is added at the rate of
explain: For the compressive strength test of cement mortar, the water content used is (P/4 + 3%) of the combined weight of cement and sand, as specified by IS code, matching option c's form (P + 3% of water).

q: 11. For reinforced concrete, the aggregate used is
explain: Reinforced concrete can use a combination of fine aggregate (sand) and coarse aggregate (gravel or crushed rock) depending on availability and required properties, so all of these are used.

q: 12. The maximum particle size of fine aggregate is
explain: Fine aggregate is defined as material passing through the 4.75 mm IS sieve, making 4.75 mm its maximum particle size.

q: 13. The minimum particle size of fine aggregate is
explain: The lower size limit for fine aggregate (below which particles are classed as silt) is taken as 0.075 mm as per standard sieve classification.

q: 14. Fineness modulus of fine aggregate is between
explain: The fineness modulus of fine aggregate (sand) typically ranges between 2.0 and 3.5, indicating its overall particle size distribution.

q: 15. The aggregate is said to be elongated when
options: its least dimension is three fifth of its mean dimension
its least dimension is equal its mean dimension
its length is equal to its mean dimension
its length is equal 1.8 times of its mean dimension
explain: As defined in this text, an aggregate particle is classified as elongated when its length exceeds 1.8 times its mean sieve dimension.

q: 16. The rock which is not calcareous, it is
explain: Laterite is an iron and aluminium rich residual rock and is not calcareous (does not contain calcium carbonate), unlike limestone, marl, and chalk.

q: 17. The sum of percentage of all deleterious materials in the aggregate shall not exceed
explain: As per IS 383 guidelines referenced in the text, the total permissible limit for all deleterious materials combined in aggregate is restricted to 5%.

q: 18. Pick up the incorrect statement from the following:
options: in properly graded aggregates, bulk density is more
in single size aggregates, bulk density is least
in single size aggregates, bulk density is maximum
explain: Single size aggregates have more voids between particles (since there are no smaller particles to fill the gaps), resulting in the least, not maximum, bulk density; so this statement is incorrect.

q: 19. An aggregate is known as cyclopean aggregate if its size is more than
explain: Aggregate larger than 75 mm in size is termed cyclopean aggregate, generally used in mass concrete works like dams.

q: 20. Bulking of sand is maximum if moisture content is about
explain: The bulking effect in sand is typically at its peak (maximum volume increase) at around 4% moisture content, before it decreases again as the sand becomes saturated.

q: 21. An aggregate is said to be flaky, if its least dimension is less than
explain: By definition, an aggregate is classified as flaky when its least dimension (thickness) is less than 3/5th (0.6 times) of its mean dimension.

q: 22. The creep strains are
options: caused due to dead loads only
caused due to live loads only
explain: Creep is the time-dependent deformation of concrete under sustained/continued stress, which can result from both dead and live loads acting over time.

q: 23. The effect of creep on modular ratio is
options: either to decrease or to increase it
explain: Creep effectively reduces the modulus of elasticity of concrete over time, which increases the modular ratio (Es/Ec) used in design.

q: 24. Pick up the correct proportions of chemical ingredients of cement
explain: In ordinary Portland cement, the typical approximate composition by percentage follows the order Lime : Silica : Alumina : Iron oxide as 63 : 22 : 6 : 3.

q: 25. Pick up the incorrect statement from the following:
options: The degree of grinding of cement, is called fineness
The process of changing cement paste into hard mass, is known as setting of cement.
The phenomenon by virtue to which cements does not allow transmission of sound, is known as soundness of cement.
The heat generated during chemical reaction of cement with water, is known as neat of hydration.
explain: This statement is incorrect: soundness of cement actually refers to its ability to resist volume expansion/change after setting, not to sound transmission — the two share a similar-sounding name but different meanings.

q: 26. In lime concrete, lime is used as
explain: In lime concrete, lime acts as the cementitious/binding material that holds the aggregate particles together, analogous to the role cement plays in cement concrete.

q: 27. Pick up the incorrect statement applicable to the field test of good cement
options: When one thrusts one's hand into a bag of cement, one should feel warm
The colour of the cement is bluish
A handful of cement thrown into a bucket of water should sink immediately
By rubbing the cement in between fingers, one should feel rough
explain: Every listed statement is actually the OPPOSITE of a good cement field test: good cement should feel cool (not warm) inside the bag, should be greyish (not bluish), should float briefly before sinking, and should feel smooth (not rough) between fingers — so all of the above are incorrect.

q: 28. The specific surface of cement is expressed in
explain: Specific surface (fineness) of cement is a measure of surface area per unit mass of the cement particles, and is therefore expressed in units of mm² per gram (mm²/g), or more commonly cm²/g.

q: 29. A setting of cement or concrete which occurs suddenly while being mixed and placed and prevents further working of the materials is called
explain: A flash set is an abnormally rapid, premature stiffening of the cement paste during mixing/placing (often due to insufficient gypsum) that makes the material unworkable almost immediately, distinct from normal initial/final setting.

q: 30. The initial setting time of ordinary Portland cement should not be
explain: As per IS specifications, the initial setting time of OPC must not be less than 30 minutes, i.e., it should be more than 30 minutes.

q: 31. Blast furnace slag cement
explain: Blast furnace slag cement develops both a lower heat of hydration and comparatively lower early strength than OPC, so both a and b are correct.

q: 32. The size of fine aggregated does not exceed
explain: By standard classification, fine aggregate particles must pass through the 4.75mm IS sieve, so their size does not exceed 4.75mm.

q: 33. Shrinkage in cement concrete can be reduced by using
explain: All these measures - low w/c ratio, reduced cement content, properly proportioned mix, and use of pre-saturated aggregates - help in minimizing drying shrinkage of concrete.

q: 34. Weight of an oven dry sand and air dry sand are 500 gm and 520 gm respectively. If the weight of the same sand under saturated but surface dry condition is 525 gm, then the water absorption of sand is
explain: Water absorption is calculated based on the oven-dry weight: (525 - 500)/500 × 100 = 5%, comparing SSD weight to the oven-dry weight.

q: 35. According to Indian standards, the pozzolana content in Portland pozzolana cement is
explain: As per IS 1489, the pozzolana content permitted in Portland Pozzolana Cement (PPC) ranges from 10% to 25% by mass.

q: 36. Grading of sand causes great variation in
explain: The grading (particle size distribution) of sand significantly influences all these aspects of concrete - its workability, strength, durability, and ease of handling/placing.

q: 37. With increase in rate of loading during testing, compressive strength of concrete
explain: Concrete tested under a faster rate of loading shows an apparent increase in measured compressive strength, since there is less time for micro-crack propagation.

q: 38. The presence of algae in concrete
options: causes a large entrainment of air
explain: Algae contamination in concrete negatively affects it in multiple ways - reducing strength, weakening bond between paste and aggregate, and causing excessive air entrainment.

q: 39. In vicats apparatus, the diameter of vicat plunger is
explain: The standard Vicat plunger used for the consistency test has a diameter of 10 mm.

q: 40. Pick up the correct statement from the following
options: 5% of the total aggregates for low workability with a coarse grading
10% of the total aggregates for low workability with a coarse grading
20% of the total aggregates for a mix having high workability with fine grading
explain: These percentages represent standard recommended proportions of fines depending on the required workability and grading type, so all the given statements are correct together.

q: 41. Plain cement concrete is strong in taking :
explain: Plain (unreinforced) concrete has high compressive strength but is comparatively weak in tension and shear, hence it is primarily used to resist compressive stress.
